# TildaZ v0.6.0

**Independent drop-down instances, each with its own config and hotkey.**

TildaZ can now run multiple fully independent drop-down terminals. Launch the
same TildaZ entry every time: the launcher restores any missing configured
workers, or opens a hotkey capture dialog when every configured worker is
already running. The implementation and user flow were verified on Linux,
macOS, and Windows. ([#267](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/267))

## Numbered instances

- The active config files are `config_0.json`, `config_1.json`, and so on.
- Each numbered config owns one worker process, global hotkey, log file, toggle
  endpoint, and desktop identity.
- A normal launch creates `config_0.json` when no numbered config exists, then
  starts every missing configured worker. Login startup starts only configs
  with `auto_start: true`.
- If all configured workers are already running, TildaZ shows worker 0 and
  opens one **Cancel / Create** hotkey capture dialog for the next instance.
- **Create** stays disabled until the captured hotkey is valid and unused by
  another TildaZ config. The conflict check runs during capture and again when
  Create is pressed.
- Bare letter, number, Space, Tab, and punctuation hotkeys are rejected to
  prevent TildaZ from taking over ordinary typing. Bare `F1` through `F12`
  remain valid.
- A legacy `config.json` is deliberately left untouched and is not loaded,
  converted, or deleted.

The launcher and workers coordinate with advisory locks in the OS runtime or
cache directory. Lock ownership, rather than a PID lookup or the presence of a
file, decides whether a worker is running. The PID stored in each lock file is
diagnostic only. See [SPEC.md](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/blob/v0.6.0/SPEC.md)
and [ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/blob/v0.6.0/ARCHITECTURE.md).

## Desktop integration

- **KDE Plasma** uses a separate KGlobalAccel component and action for every
  instance.
- **GNOME and Cinnamon** track numbered configs and windows through their Shell
  extensions, with numbered GSettings entries as the fallback path.
- **COSMIC and Hyprland** synchronize only the difference between configured
  TildaZ bindings and current compositor bindings.
- **sway** registers each numbered binding through IPC. sway does not expose a
  binding query API, so a binding removed from config may remain until the sway
  session restarts.
- **macOS and Windows** register each worker's hotkey independently. While the
  creation dialog captures a new shortcut, existing TildaZ hotkeys are
  temporarily suspended so the dialog receives the key instead of toggling a
  worker.

The prompt now uses the same capture behavior on every platform: no text input
box, immediate canonical shortcut display, red conflict feedback, and the
same **Cancel / Create** order. Linux testing covered KDE Plasma, GNOME,
Cinnamon, COSMIC, Hyprland, and sway. macOS and Windows were also verified on
real systems. Test records and implementation decisions are preserved in
[#267](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/267).

## Upgrade notes

v0.6.0 intentionally does not migrate the old unnumbered `config.json`. On the
first v0.6.0 launch, TildaZ creates a new `config_0.json` with current defaults,
including the `F1` hotkey and 15-point logical terminal font. Keep the old file
as a reference if you want to reapply custom settings manually.

On macOS, ad-hoc development builds still receive a new signing hash after a
rebuild, which can invalidate Input Monitoring and Accessibility permissions.
Local developers can use the stable `TildazLocal` identity documented in
[`dist/macos/SETUP.md`](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/blob/v0.6.0/dist/macos/SETUP.md).

## Downloads

| Platform | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Linux portable (glibc 2.28+) | `tildaz-v0.6.0-linux-{x86_64,aarch64}.tar.gz` | Extract and run `./install.sh`; no `sudo`. |
| Linux Debian / Ubuntu | `tildaz_0.6.0_{amd64,arm64}.deb` | Install with `dpkg` or a graphical software installer. |
| Linux Fedora / RHEL / openSUSE | `tildaz-0.6.0-1.{x86_64,aarch64}.rpm` | Install with `dnf` or the distro package tool. |
| Linux distro-independent | `TildaZ-0.6.0-{x86_64,aarch64}.AppImage` | Make executable and run; FUSE is optional. |
| Arch / Manjaro / EndeavourOS | `tildaz-0.6.0-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst` | x86_64 package. |
| macOS 14+ universal | `tildaz-v0.6.0-macos.dmg` | Apple Silicon and Intel; ad-hoc signed. |
| Windows 10/11 x64 | `tildaz-v0.6.0-win-x64.zip` | Includes the bundled ConPTY runtime. |
| Windows 11 ARM64 | `tildaz-v0.6.0-win-arm64.zip` | ARM64-native binary and ConPTY runtime. |

## Known limitations

- [#249](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/249): a macOS NSAlert can very
  rarely require a second Enter or Esc press because of accessory-app key-window
  timing.
- [#266](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/266): headless Windows ConPTY
  does not expose OSC 10/11 default colors, so `fish_terminal_color_theme` may
  remain empty in WSL. `COLORFGBG` is still supplied from the TildaZ theme.
- [#244](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/244): switching between KDE
  Plasma and another desktop in one user session can leave the XDG Desktop
  Portal backend wedged until its user services restart.
- Linux remains Wayland-only and currently uses a correct software `wl_shm`
  renderer. GPU renderer work is tracked in
  [#277](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/277).
